fragment.claim_boundary: Exactly one two-task held-out grid-reasoning adaptation trial; no broad continual-learning, autonomy, production, AGI, user-level, upper-objective, or monitor-completion inference.
fragment.purpose: Select one externally anchored, contamination-controlled sequential-transfer unit that is materially different from the completed matched-evidence guard.

observations: A materially different next unit should test observable cross-task adaptation rather than another continuation-integrity mechanism.
Sequential-transfer evidence requires outcome isolation, a frozen baseline, a bounded learning record, and a fresh adapted context.
Two held-out tasks can falsify one narrow adaptation claim but cannot establish broad continual learning or AGI.

result.continuation: Independently Task Evaluate the exact precommit order, contamination exclusions, baseline and adapted predictions, holder reveals, deterministic scores, all negative controls, replay identity, and external source provenance; then continue Candidate Evaluate, Consolidate, Learn, Root, and materially different safe work while the upper objective remains unmet.
expected_outputs: A precommit receipt binding source commit, license, selector, both task identities, holder commitments, scoring rule, and contamination exclusions
Immutable baseline predictions for task A and task B before either held-out output is revealed
A bounded task-A learning record with an explicit non-answer-bearing claim boundary
One adapted task-B prediction made before its held-out output is revealed
Deterministic exact-cell and exact-grid scores for baseline task B versus adapted task B
Pass, fail, or uncertain verdict for this one sequential-transfer unit, including every negative control and replay digest
Zero upstream writes, Candidate activation false, and AGI, user-level, and upper-objective verdicts unchanged
result.goal: Run one precommitted, held-out sequential-transfer trial on exactly two previously unused ARC-style grid tasks from a permissively licensed public repository at an immutable commit: solve both once with the same frozen baseline, extract one bounded non-answer-bearing rule from the first task only, then re-solve the second task with that persisted rule and determine whether exact held-out accuracy improves without harming fail-closed controls.
inputs_and_evidence_needed: An exact public repository commit and license for an ARC-style dataset not previously used by this execution
A deterministic selector that freezes exactly two same-family tasks before any held-out test outputs are read
Training input/output examples and held-out test inputs for both tasks, with test outputs held by an isolated reveal step
One frozen baseline solver context used independently for task A and task B
One persisted learning record derived only from task A's revealed result and prohibited from containing task B answer cells
A fresh task-B solver context receiving only the original task-B training examples plus that bounded learning record
Negative controls for leaked answer cells, changed task identity, changed source commit, mismatched holder commitment, and duplicate replay
result.scope: A single two-task external grid-reasoning trial measuring narrow cross-task adaptation. It must not be generalized to broad continual learning, production autonomy, AGI, user-level completion, or upper-objective completion.
success_criteria: All source, task, holder, and scoring commitments precede outcome-bearing reveal
No task-B test output or answer-bearing derivative enters the adapted solver context
The adapted task-B exact score strictly exceeds the frozen baseline task-B score
Every declared leakage, identity, source-clock, holder, and replay negative control fails closed
The result remains bounded to two selected tasks and does not support an AGI claim
